chapter: Boyhood and the West End camps
title: Opening of the 1961 interview at the French Market Fisherman Supplies
summary: Interviewers give the date and place and mention a young trumpeter also named Louis Armstrong who studied with Pritchett; Artigues is asked his name.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: A real one, December 15, 1961. We're recording today at French Market Fisherman Supplies, 813 Decatur Street. What's your name? Paul Crawford. And mine's Dick Allen. We're waiting on Albert Artighe. He's talking to young Louis Armstrong downstairs, a trumpet player who happens to have the same name as the original Louis Armstrong. While it's fresh in my mind, I thought I'd add that young Louis Armstrong says he's some sort of little off cousin to the original Louis Armstrong. Says that when he first got started, he played some with George Lewis. He had an old man, I believe it was Armstrong's band, not George Lewis's, had an old man called Kaiser, John Joseph's brother, Willie Joseph, also in the band. And when he was young, what is that, about 14 or 16? 14 I believe it was. He talked to Elmer Talbot. We sent him to see Professor Pritchett, who was loaded, he said. I presume he meant that he was full of students. And Pritchett's University Professor Delmont, who taught him. First thing I want to know is your name. Albert Artighe. That's with a S on the end? Yeah. A-R-T-I-G-U-E-S. Mm-hmm. I see. Now the embarrassing questions. When were you born?
